senses.gloss: ch. (= h. יָרֵחַ a. יֶרַח) moon; month.—יומא די׳ or י׳ (sub. ריש) the first day of the month, New-Moon-Day.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 47:13">Targ. Is. XLVII, 13</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 20:18">Targ. I Sam. XX, 18</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 46:1">Targ. Ez. XLVI, 1</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 21:13">Targ. O. Deut. XXI, 13</cite> <he>יִרַח יומין</he> ed. Berl. (oth. ed. <cite ref="J00624"><he>יְרַח</he></cite>; Y. <he>תלתא יַרְחִין</he>).—

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 29:9">Lev. R. s. 29</cite>; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 40:1">Pesik. R. s. 40</cite> (ref. to <he>בחדש השביעי</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 23:24">Lev. XXIII, 24</cite>) <he>בי׳ דשבועתא</he> in the month of oaths (<cite ref="Genesis 22:16">Gen. XXII, 16</cite>).
<cite ref="Shabbat 86b:5">Sabb. 86ᵇ</cite> <he>בחד בשבא איקבע י׳</he> the New-Moon was declared on the first day of the week.
<cite ref="Shabbat 86b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>פליגי בקביע די׳</he> they differ as to the day on which the New Moon was declared.

<cite ref="Beitzah 4b:12">Bets. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>והשתא דידעינן בקביעא די׳</he> and now that we know the time of the New Moon (by fixed calendar); a. fr.—Pl. <he>יַרְחִין</he>, <he>יַרְחַיָּא</he>, <he>יַרְחֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 1:14">Targ. Y. Gen. I, 14</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 2:2">Targ. Ex. II, 2</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 20a:18">R. Hash. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>בשאר י׳</he> as to the other months (than Nisan and Tishri). Y. ib. II, 57ᵈ bot.
<cite ref="Makkot 23b:15">Macc. 23ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>תריסר ירחי שתא</he> twelve months (forming) a year, twelve months from date.
